claims.claim: Fabrication inherently involves a Promethean revolt and the destruction of nature because homo faber creates a man-made world by destroying part of God-created nature.
claims.supporting_excerpt: This element of violation and violence is present in all fabrication and homo faber , the creator of human artifice, has always been a destroyer of nature.

claims.claim: In the second phase of modernity, the victorious rise of animal laborans leads to natural processes flooding and annihilating the lasting artificial constructions of the human world.
claims.supporting_excerpt: Natural processes are flooding the lasting artificial constructions of human existence. Their Trojan horse, paradoxically, is the same technological productivity which has created the world of lasting things; in the second phase of modernity it annihilates its own creature.

definitions.definition: The creator of human artifice who conducts himself as lord and master of the whole Earth, objectifies everything, and whose construction of the human world involves an over-all reification of nature.
The entity that embodies the natural part of human being, ensuring the futile, perishable goods of consumption needed for mere biological survival, remaining the servant of nature and the Earth.

distinctions.distinction: Animal laborans remains the servant of nature and the Earth nourishing life with its body, whereas homo faber conducts himself as lord and master of the whole Earth and acts as a destroyer of nature through fabrication.

must_not_be_lost: Fabrication launches artificial processes or stops natural processes depending on the fabricator's aim.
Productivity in Arendt's thought is interpreted as a special form of fertility and a natural force embodied in human labor.
parsed.segment_function: Analyzing the role of homo faber, fabrication, and the shift toward animal laborans in Arendt's interpretation of modernity and nature.
